terms.gloss: drawn to one’s own sex: gay
evidence: M-O s.v. homosexual, gay (after Suet. Galb. 22: libīdinis in marēs prōnior)
terms.comment: Morgan–Owens’s phrase, built on Suetonius. For a man amōris in marēs prōnior, for a woman amōris in fēminās prōnior (M-O). In conversation a plain clause says it as well: virōs amat, fēminās amat. Classical Latin has no neutral word; the old sense of English gay, cheerful, is hilaris or laetus (see cheerful).
An insult in Plautus, Catullus and Juvenal, and so also a lewd dancer (Lewis & Short); never a neutral word for a gay man.

sources: Lewis & Short: pronus · Lewis & Short: cinaedus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. homosexual man, gay man; homosexual woman, lesbian; homosexual, gay.
